newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end up ahead of Chidambaram's speech.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end up ahead of Chidambaram's speech.

text.p: Bombay shares ended higher on Monday driven by hopes Indian Finance Minister Chidambaram would offer incentives to retail and institutional investors, traders said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange closed 49.85 points or 1.42 percent higher at a provisional 3564.46.
Chidambaram's reply to a debate on the federal budget for 1996/97 (April-March) is scheduled for Tuesday. He plans to make a more detailed reply to the finance bill on September 9 or 10.
The finance minister assured institutional investors at a recent meeting some changes in the budget proposals would be implemented fairly quickly, market sources said.
Some analysts expect a dilution in the controversial 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax (MAT) announced in the budget.
"Export earnings may be exempt from MAT," one analyst said.
But an institutional investor present at the meeting with Chidambaram said it was unlikely he would change tax proposals.
"There may not be anything drastic on the tax front but he is likely to announce some sops for investors," he said.

Chidambaram's speech -- originally scheduled for Monday -- was postponed when the lower house of the Indian parliament was adjourned without transacting any business on Monday due to the death of a member.
"Hopes of an announcement from Chidambaram have been pushing the market higher for a while now. We are likely to see a bit of a correction soon," said a trader at a local brokerage.
Expectations of changes drove the 30-share index 83.21 points or 2.42 percent higher to 3514.61 in the week to Friday.
Traders said some U.S. funds were absent from the market on a public holiday.
Nestle India said its 1996 first half net rose marginally to 223 million rupees from 222 million rupees a year ago. Nestle shares fell 9.50 rupees to 274.
